lineComments: Split into three sentences: when it fires, what to filter on, what it carries.
rows.replacement: After each sync the app broadcasts an intent. Your automation app can filter on the action below to start a profile. The intent carries the record count and the time, and fires at most once a minute.

rows.comment: Em dash, "not a setting" rebuttal nobody raised, punchy fragments.
lineComments: State the limit and its cause once.
rows.replacement: iOS cannot start a shortcut when a sync finishes. Shortcuts personal automations trigger only on Apple's fixed list of events, and apps cannot add to it. Android supports this.

rows.comment: Privacy statement kept: no readiness, strain or sleep score. Cut the em dash, the aphoristic closing line and the rule-of-three feel.
lineComments: Keep the exclusion; give the reason (absent metrics become zero) and what is sent.
rows.replacement: The broadcast never includes readiness, strain or sleep score, on either platform. An absent metric would arrive as a bare zero, so only sync facts go out: the record count and the time.

rows.comment: Curly quotes; second sentence is a hypothetical. State the token's purpose.
lineComments: Straight quotes and a direct purpose statement.
rows.replacement: Send wtf.openstrap.openstrap_edge.BUZZ_STRAP with this token as the "token" string extra. The token stops other apps on the phone from buzzing your band.

rows.comment: Colon connector and "what it cannot do" fragment.
rows.replacement: On iOS, a shortcut you run yourself can buzz the band. It cannot run automatically when the band syncs.
No token yet. Reopen this screen.

lineComments: "Switched off for this app" is indirect.

rows.comment: Rebuts a worry about the band ("this is not the band") and uses an em dash. The fix line already tells the user what to do.
lineComments: State the cause and consequence only.
rows.replacement: Without Bluetooth permission, OpenStrap cannot scan for or connect to the band.

rows.comment: Semicolon and "nothing is lost" assurance; say what the band does.
lineComments: Cause, then what the band does meanwhile.
rows.replacement: Bluetooth is off on the phone, so no app can reach the band. The band keeps recording and holds the data until you reconnect.
The band connects only over Bluetooth Low Energy, so this phone cannot sync it live. Imported data still works.
Reconnecting is paused

rows.comment: Long single sentence with a "rather than" clause. Split it and keep the plural block exactly.

Pair the band again

rows.comment: Dense; split cause and effect. Keep the data-safety reassurance as a fact.
lineComments: Active verbs, one idea per sentence.
rows.replacement: The band connects but rejects the phone's encryption key, so it drops every command and sends no data. Your recordings stay on the band.

rows.comment: Em dash and "nothing is lost" repetition.
lineComments: Cause, saved status, what blocks the band.
rows.replacement: The band keeps re-sending the same batch because the app's confirmation does not reach it. The batch is already saved here. The band cannot move on until the confirmation arrives.

rows.comment: Redundant reassurance ("still on the band and still safe; it just is not").
rows.replacement: The band reports newer recordings than it will send. They are still on the band.

lineComments: Symptom, likely cause, what the app does.
rows.replacement: Each sync finishes with no sensor readings. This usually means the band's clock is out of sync. The app resets the clock on every connect.

rows.comment: Lists real causes and one useful fact.

rows.replacement: Detects each heartbeat from the electrical signal (the R-peak of each beat).

lineComments: Define both terms on first use.
rows.replacement: Pulse, sleep and temperature around the clock. Beat timing comes from the optical pulse wave, so heart rate variability (HRV) here is pulse rate variability (PRV).
Steps from the phone's motion coprocessor. It records no other metrics.
